subject: Tenant egress and staging proxy constraints for Private VPC PoC

Subject: Private deployment: tenant egress & staging proxy constraints

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at NovaCloud is excited to move into a short PoC to validate a Private VPC deployment. Before we lock in an on-site staging window (week of Apr 12), we need to confirm a couple of network/architecture constraints so our networking and procurement teams can prepare. I attached our requirements PDF.

High-level asks:
- We need a recommended pattern for tenant egress from customer VPC to Redwood (data plane) that preserves source IPs where possible.
- For the control plane (management plane) calls back to Redwood, we need to validate mutual TLS and cert rotation cadence.
- In staging we want an ingress/proxy in our VPC to centralize outbound filtering; curious if Redwood supports a dual-proxy pattern (customer egress proxy + Redwood relay).
- Any special port ranges, health-check CIDRs, or BGP/static routing expectations?

Can you loop in infra/ops folks? Would appreciate a short architecture sketch and recommended options by EOD Thu so we can share with our SecOps. Meeting depending on your availability: Thurs Apr 2, 10:00–11:00 PT?

Attachments: nova_poc_network_requirements.pdf

Thanks,
Maya R.

NovaCloud, Inc.

Subject: Re: Private deployment: tenant egress & staging proxy constraints

Maya — thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. Looping in Jonas (infra) and Neha (ops) so we can give you a concise set of options. Quick notes up front while we draft a brief diagram:

1) Recommended patterns (short):
   - Option A (preferred for most customers): Customer-managed egress proxy in their VPC that forwards to Redwood via a secured egress relay (Redwood accepts from one or more static IP ranges). Preserves source if you use X-Forwarded-For + proxy-preserved headers; SNAT possible if you need it.
   - Option B (dual-proxy / relay): Your staging proxy -> Redwood relay -> internal service mesh. Useful when you require centralized filtering + DLP inspection in staging. Adds one hop but centralizes controls.
   - Option C (Direct peering / private interconnect): For larger deployments, private interconnect (VPC peering/Direct Connect) for source-IP preservation without SNAT. This requires route-exchange and procurement lead time.

2) Control plane: we require mutual TLS for control-plane RPCs. Cert rotation: recommend 90-day rotation by default; we support automated rotation via customer-managed CA or Redwood-managed with rotation hooks.

3) Ports/healthchecks: generally 443 for control-plane mTLS, and 1024–65535 ephemeral for data sessions if you expect client-initiated outbound flows. For health checks use 443 from Redwood health IP set (we'll provide exact CIDRs).

Next step: Jonas will sketch the proxy/egress diagram and call out route/SNAT details; Neha will outline runbook items for staging cutover. If Apr 2 at 10:00 PT works we can do a 30-min sync.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
olga@redwoodinference.com
From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com

Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 07:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: tenant egress & staging proxy constraints

Thanks — I put together a quick draw.io diagram and a short checklist (see Drive link below). Highlights and actionables from infra perspective:

- SNAT vs. source-preserve: If you need true source preservation for backend audit logs, use private interconnect or configure your egress proxies to preserve source and advertise specific /32s to us. If that's not possible, we'll accept SNATed flows from a small set of Elastic IPs (we'll publish them).
- BGP vs static: BGP is preferred for dynamic route failover. Static routes are fine for short-lived PoC but expect manual intervention on failover.
- Healthchecks: TCP/443 from our health CIDR: 34.201.0.0/16 (example). We'll provide the final list and rotation window.
- TLS: mTLS for control plane, TLS1.2+ for data plane. We support ACME-managed certs on the relay and can integrate with your internal CA if needed.

Staging checklist (short):
  - Create staging VPC and attach egress proxy (iptables/nginx/haproxy)
  - Provide a service account for Redwood and an allowlist of egress IPs
  - Confirm whether SNAT is acceptable for PoC or if we need a NAT-exempt path
  - Share expected QPS and burst (we need to size relay)

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExample (contains tenant-egress-proxy-arch.drawio)

Attachment: tenant-egress-proxy-arch.drawio

- Cert rotation: 90 days is fine but Alex asks if you support short-notice rotation (we may need emergency revoke).
- QPS: initial PoC will be ~150 qps sustained with ~700 qps bursts.

We can meet Fri Apr 3 at 16:00 PT if that works for you to finalize the runbook. I've attached the procurement contact and updated requirements.

Regards,
Maya
